Something sort of like what you describe happened to me once.

This is like late 90s early 00s, and me and a buddy were in my car driving from A to B. We're going along, minding our business, on a mostly empty road in the late afternoon - nobody behind me, and really nobody in front of me, with only an occasional car in the oncoming lane. Out of nowhere comes a Sheriff car, doing every bit of 100MPH (in a 45 or 50MPH zone) and he doesn't have his flashers on. He came out from behind the car in the opposite lane to pass what was in front of him, and now he's bearing down on me.

I took me a second to realize what was happening, which means it took me a second to react. At the very last instant before we were all dead, I swerved to the right and put my car through a ditch, jumped up out of the ditch, over a driveway, almost hit like three trees, almost hit one of those little shacks that kids wait for the school bus in, went back into and then back out of the ditch, jumping right back on the road still doing 45 to 50MPH, and we kept on our way like nothing happened.

In that first instant when I swerved into the ditch, the cop and my eyes met. We were both wearing sunglasses, but I knew we were looking eye to eye. And I believe that I got a flash from his mind to mine - "Sorry, citizen! Life or death! Out of the way!" It wasn't so much words as a feeling, but that's what the feeling meant.

As I was doing my miracle driving, I saw the whole thing happening from the driver's seat, from the passenger's seat, from the back seat, from a few feet above the car, from where I went into the ditch, from where I came back out of it, and from every point and every angle at every instant in between. I saw the whole path my car would take through the ditch and the trees and back through the ditch like it was a big red metal and glass snake slithering through the woods. I saw when I had to turn the wheel and by how much. I knew never to change my foot on the gas pedal and not to touch the clutch or the brakes.

That wasn't the first time I had an experience like that, and it wasn't the last, but it was definitely the most memorable.
